 By Audrey Noble October 28, 2026 Smile Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story If scalp care is haircare, then we know to turn to K-beauty for the ultimate hair washing routine. But its approach goes beyond innovative ingredients and cleansing techniques to get strong and sleek strands. As Beth Stokes, associate director of marketing at Dr. Groot, explains, the Korean way to wash hair is a more holistic and preventative philosophy than Western hair washing routines, which solely focus on the cleansing part. “It prioritizes the scalp as the foundation for healthy, resilient hair,” says Stokes. “Treating it much like skin.”
 “Korean beauty has helped make scalp care feel like an important part of self-care and a daily routine, rather than something you only think about when you develop problems like dandruff, itching, or hair thinning,” adds Y. Claire Chang , MD, board-certified dermatologist at Union Derm. “Instead of focusing only on making the hair look shinier or smoother, the approach considers both scalp health and hair health as connected.”
 To wash your hair the Korean way, consider the following:
 The Staple Ingredients
 One can expect to see many skincare ingredients along with traditional Korean hair ingredients in shampoos, scalp scrubs, conditioners, and masks. These can include salicylic acid, niacinamide, centella, and panthenol, says Sarah Chung Park , founder and CEO of Landing International, and black bean, black sesame, kelp, and rice water. And with newer formulations, she says that PDRN and exosomes are moving to scalp ampoules to better support healthy hair growth. The goals, she says, are the same as for your face: clean, calm, and balanced.
 “Your scalp is skin,” says Park. “It gets oily, dry, irritated, and it ages, just like your face. Korean consumers already know so much about skincare that taking care of the scalp feels like the natural next step.”
 Hair Vinegar
 Vinegar rinses have been around for years in Korean hair care as a traditional home remedy, but aren’t really a staple today. Though the acetic acid in vinegar is known to smooth the hair’s surface and add shine, Stokes says the effect is temporary and there’s little scientific evidence to show that it can improve scalp health or help with hair regrowth .
 “What’s popular now is ‘hair vinegar,’” says Park. “[It’s] a product made just for the scalp. You apply it after shampooing, massage it in, and rinse. Koreans love it for oily scalps, buildup, and scalp odor, which gets worse in hot, humid summers.”
 The Process
 Each hair wash routine will differ based on your personal needs, but generally speaking, a Korean hair wash routine includes the following steps:
 A Scalp Pre-Treatment Dr. Chang says that this is an occasional step and something you won’t need for every wash. But some people will use some sort of scalp scaler or exfoliating treatment before shampooing to help remove excess sebum, dead skin cells, and product buildup.
 Targeted Shampoo Dr. Chang says that shampoo is typically chosen based on scalp concerns (think excess oil, sensitivity, flaking, etc.) rather than just thinking about dry or damaged hair. So you’ll pick formulations that will incorporate soothing ingredients to support scalp health. Park says that you’ll wash hair with lukewarm water and massage it in for about a minute. “A lot of Koreans use a silicone scalp brush for this,” she adds. “It cleans more deeply and feels like a mini head massage.”
 Korean shampoos are having a moment in the States. She points to products like the Lador Tea Tree Calming Scalp Shampoo , which uses tea tree oil and menthol to control excess sebum and flakes while also provides the scalp with a nice cooling sensation, or the Lilyeve Grow:Turn Shampoo , to support scalp help over time.
 Conditioning Hair Treatment “These focus on improving softness, smoothness, and manageability while reducing friction and breakage,” says Dr. Chang. She says that you’ll typically apply them to mid-lengths and the ends of the hair, unless specifically formulated for the scalp. You can also use the occasional intensive treatments, such as a hair mask, protein treatment, scalp packs, or vinegar-based rinse.
 Celebrity hairstylist Mark Townsend , who says he didn’t see true innovation in the scalp care space until using K-beauty products, loves the Dr. Groot Miracle In Shower Scalp & Hydrating Treatment . Made to be used after shampooing, it contains salicylic acid, rosemary oil, and biotin to hydrate hair, exfoliate the scalp, and promote healthy hair growth. “Star of the show,” he says. “The results have been incredible. My clients that have switched over to the Dr. Groot shampoos and treatment have seen a major improvement in the health of their hair which makes styling so much easier for me.”
 You’ll end your hair routine with a leave-in scalp tonic or serum, that she says is meant to add more targeted activities to address specific scalp concerns. Then, without adding excessive heat or friction, dry the scalp thoroughly. If these steps and all these products are too overwhelming to start, no worries. Park says you can just focus on these three steps to wash hair the Korean way: “A good scalp shampoo, a treatment, and drying your scalp completely,” she says.
